messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl2-disc] plot_pxg
messages.body_plain:
The labels are taken from the input genotypes.
If you are using

  plot_pxg(geno, phenotype, sort=FALSE)

then the labels are taken from the contents of geno. If it's a factor, the labels will be the factor levels. If it's a vector of character strings, it'll be the unique values.

So you need to turn your AA/BB/CC values into strain names.

  str <- c("Bur", "Can", "Col", ...)

  # replace factor levels
  levels(geno) <- str

  # or if it's not a factor...
  n_str <- length(str)
  ordered_values <- paste0(LETTERS[1:n_str], LETTERS[1:n_str])
  geno <- str[ match(geno, ordered_values) ]

Note that the names of the founders may be as row names in the founder genotypes:

  str <- rownames(arab$founder_geno[[1]])

In the development version of R/qtl2, there's a function founders() that can pull these out:

  str <- founders(arab)

karl

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl2-disc] Founder representation plot
messages.body_plain:
Use calc_geno_freq() to get genotype or allele frequencies. Use plot_scan1() to plot them.
Here's an example.

   doex <- read_cross2("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rqtl/qtl2data/master/DOex/DOex.zip" <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rqtl/qtl2data/master/DOex/DOex.zip>)
   pr <- calc_genoprob(doex, error_prob=0.002, map_function="c-f", cores=0)
   apr <- genoprob_to_alleleprob(pr)
   af <- calc_geno_freq(apr, "marker", omit_x=FALSE)
   par(mfrow=c(8,1), mar=c(2.1, 4.1, 0.6, 0.6))
   ymax <- max(af)
   for(i in 1:8) plot_scan1(af, doex$pmap, lod=i, ylab=colnames(af)[i], ylim=c(0, ymax))

To get heterozygosities of the raw SNP genotypes, there's a function calc_raw_het() in the development version of R/qtl2.
You can get access to it by sourcing the github file:

   source("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rqtl/qtl2/master/R/calc_raw_summaries.R" <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rqtl/qtl2/master/R/calc_raw_summaries.R>)
   snphet <- calc_raw_het(doex, "marker")

You can plot the results with plot_scan1(), but you need to convert it to a matrix, for example with cbind():

   plot_scan1( cbind(snphet), doex$pmap)

karl

Hi Kurl

We are running a 4way mapping population with multiple sites in qtl2. We previously discussed how to convert the probability from qtl to qtl2. We stacked the probability of 750 individuals for 19 sites and calculate the kinship . We then run a QTL model with kinship and use site as a covariate. Right now we are running this only for one phenotype "BIOMASS"

out_full = scan1(probs2, pheno, addcovar = covariate, intcovar = covariate, kinship = kinship_loco_multiple, cores=5)

This model runs perfectly in our local server but takes almost 25 GB of RAM in each core. To make it faster we tried to run it on TACC cluster and we ended up with output that has negative LOD scores. To fix this issue, right now we are running only with two sites and this is the summary of scan1 we got for two sites:

> out_full = scan1(probs2, pheno, addcovar = covariate, intcovar = covariate, kinship = kinship_loco_multiple, cores=5)

    BIOMASS

 1st Qu.:-156.77
 Median : -91.95
 Mean   :-106.54
 3rd Qu.: -42.54
 Max.   :   2.44

But if I remove additive and interactive cov if looks normal:

> out_full = scan1(probs2, pheno, kinship = kinship_loco_multiple, cores=5)
> summary(out_full)
    BIOMASS
 Min.   :0.00426
 1st Qu.:0.36295
 Median :0.76280
 Mean   :1.17617
 3rd Qu.:1.56336
 Max.   :7.75820

What is your thoughts for this issue?

Thanks!

Best,
Taslima
